substantive_reconstruction.leading_coefficient: In R[t], (1-t)^(k+1) has nonzero leading coefficient (-1)^(k+1) and degree k+1. Multiplication by the monic t^i shifts degree by i and leaves that coefficient unchanged. Exact degree is i+k+1; k=i=1 yields t-2t^2+t^3, degree3 rather than2. With 0<=i<=k, it is at most d=2k+1, equal to d iff i=k. It is never zero or constant, since k+1>=1. The question's ambient Bernstein degree does not assert exact degree of every represented polynomial.
substantive_reconstruction.binomial_denominator_and_factorization: For 0<=j<=k-i, r=i+j<=k<=2k+1=d, so choose(d,r)>0. Cancelling this binomial in w B is legitimate and yields choose(k-i,j)t^(i+j)(1-t)^(d-i-j). Since d-i-j=(k+1)+(k-i-j), factor out t^i(1-t)^(k+1). The remaining sum is (t+(1-t))^(k-i)=1, proving the displayed identity for all real t with no division by t or 1-t.
substantive_reconstruction.source_coefficients_and_collection: The source coefficientSeries is exp(t)*(1-t)^(-(k+1)); its degree-i coefficient is sum_{m=0}^i choose(k+i-m,k)/m!, exactly a_{k,i}. Each summand is nonnegative over the reals, with factorial denominator positive. The truncation keeps i=0..k, so endpointFactor is F. Collecting the elevated terms assigns L_r=sum_{i,j}[r=i+j]a_i w_ij, with zero support above k; every L_r is nonnegative.
substantive_reconstruction.reflection_and_source_bridge: B_{d,r}(1-t)=B_{d,d-r}(t) follows from choose(d,r)=choose(d,d-r) and swapping the powers. Reindex the finite d+1 term sum to get F(1-t)=sum_r L_(d-r)B_{d,r}(t). Therefore c_r=exp(-1)L_r+L_(d-r), with nonnegative coefficients independent of t. The source's taylor1 evaluates the weighted expression at p+1; at p=t-1 this is precisely H(t), not a weight-swapped target.
substantive_reconstruction.endpoints_and_degenerate_indices: i=k leaves j=0 with w=1/choose(d,k), already at actual degree d. i=0 has actual degree k+1. k=0 forces i=j=0,d=1,F=1-t and coefficients(exp(-1),1), giving H=exp(-1)(1-t)+t. At t=0 or1 all formulas remain polynomial identities, with exponent-zero factors1; no analytical 0^0 limit is introduced. In fact H(0)=exp(-1),H(1)=1 for every k because a_(k,0)=1. Negative or outside-unit t does not break the identity, but nonnegative basis values are only used on [0,1].
substantive_reconstruction.nonnegativity_and_resource_boundary: On [0,1], t and 1-t are nonnegative, making every Bernstein basis value nonnegative. Nonnegative c_r then imply H>=0. No claim of sign outside the interval, numerical coefficient stability, finite-bit efficiency or quantum state/circuit realization follows. The leading-degree reasoning is independently derived NL algebra; elevation/source-bridge theorem bodies were read but not rerun.
